messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] pool() function usage
messages.body_plain:
Dear Atongo,

pool() is something used to condense the number of samples in a methylBase object (obtained from unite()). I will explain it with the following example

> meth_red
methylBase object with 685577 rows
--------------
   chr  start    end strand coverage1 numCs1 numTs1 coverage2 numCs2 numTs2 coverage3 numCs3 numTs3 coverage4 numCs4 numTs4
1 chr1  10497  10497      +        70     68      2        47     45      2        47     47      0        57     54      3
2 chr1  10525  10525      +        70     70      0        47     46      1        45     42      3        56     56      0
--------------
sample.ids: n_h7_s14_p15 n_h7_s14_p23 abn_h7_s6_p117 abn_h7_s6_p113
destranded FALSE
assembly: hg19
context: CpG
treament: 0 0 1 1
resolution: base
> pool(meth_red, c("new","old"))
methylBase object with 685577 rows

The above 'meth_red' is a methylbase object with total 4 samples (2 for each treatment)

Now using pool() one can condense this data groupwise. That means simply add up (as far as I understood) counts (coverage1+coverage2; numCs1+numC2...........) for each sample belonging to the same treatment and create a single. Finally you will create a new methylabase

> pool(meth_red, c("new","old"))
methylBase object with 685577 rows
--------------
   chr  start    end strand coverage1 numCs1 numTs1 coverage2 numCs2 numTs2
1 chr1  10497  10497      +       117    113      4       104    101      3
2 chr1  10525  10525      +       117    116      1       101     98      3
--------------
sample.ids: new old
destranded FALSE
assembly: hg19
context: CpG
treament: 0 1
resolution: base

here you can see that coverage1 (117=70+47). So are the other counts.
Hope this explanation helps

ᐧ

Regards,
Kalyan

messages.body_plain:
Dear Juan,

the diffmeth analysis performed on refseq bed file (gene.obj) contains list of promoters, introns, exons and TSS. So, number of rows is the sum of overlaps among all the genic parts and not just genes.

The default methylKit analysis gives a decent understanding of the differential methylation across the genome mapped by the sequencing data. One can easily move from methylKit into other bioconductor libraries to extract the actual list of promoters, exons, introns etc., MethylKit provides some useful function in this regard. Questions on similar lines were previously asked in this forum and have been discussed.

You may go through one such discussion here: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/methylkit_discussion/1cTdqCLFlqc.

ᐧ

Regards,
Kalyan

Dear Raza,

I am not sure if one can do this in methylKit yet. But before considering to do that, one may consider the fact that methylation atleast in human genomes is highly contextual. This means that methylation is mostly (~99%) is observed at CpG only and not in other contexts. Also  note that the functions that operate of CpGs can not be used in other contexts eg., merging strand coverage from + and - strand.

Regards,
Kalyan

messages.subject: Christmas offer for researchers interested in methylomics
messages.subject_clean: Christmas offer for researchers interested in methylomics
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

The coming week is going to be a vacation and most of us are going on vacation. Me too. However, I thought that this Christmas I would OFFER fellow researchers a GOOD service.

Many of the methylKit users are biologists learning to deal with their sequencing data. I also started just like you and spent hours and days learning R/Bioconductor related packages. Now, I thought I would offer the skills I have developed at most affordable price for the researchers (actually, my service is FREE, I collect charges only to PREVENT SPAM requests and some of it will go into developing further resources to help users like you)

Here are the details of my christmas offer: I am now offering methylation analysis for two samples (1 control and 1 test). As part of my offering I would get the following done for you:
QC report of the FASTQ reads
Mapping (hg19/mm10) using BISMARK
Bisulfite efficiency analysis (if you have used lambda spike in)
MethylKit workflow to suit your needs
Additional workflow in bioconductor to extract the list of genic elements/or non-genic elements with differentially methylated CpGs
Not only this, I also offer 30min - 1 hr consultation on planning methylome experiments (RRBS/WGBS). Yes, you have heard right, I do data analysis and I build NGS libraries my self. So, I can help you planning experiments. I have built and sequenced over 100 RRBS libraries and 10 WGBS libraries from 10ng - 30ng DNA (I have NOT heard of any commercial service provider offering methylomes from such smaller amounts of DNA). So, with my tips you can build libraries from very precious samples. I know the ins and outs of NGS library prep and good understanding of methylation analysis. I can see the QC and tell you what has gone wrong in the library prep (if there is any).

Price details:
RRBS/WGBS consultation (Sample processing, library prep, data analysis) for 30min to 1 hr : $15 for 30 min (only 3 slots)
RRBS data analysis as mentioned above : $ 50 (only 10 slots)
I will also explain you the pipeline and the results will be delivered in neatly explained document/ppt. If necessary over skype/hangout
WGBS data analysis : $50 (only 1 slot)
WGBS analysis will NOT cover the above data analysis due to huge cost of time and computational resources. I will do QC report, mapping and bisulfite efficiency analysis only.
Risk Free Service:
After experiencing this service if you feel that my expertise is not useful for you, I WILL RETURN 80% of the price you PAID with NO QUESTIONS ASKED. All you have to do is just ask for your money. I am sure people reading this forum are true to their conscience. I can not return 100% because I will be doing it on hired infrastructure on CLOUD
If you happen to use the results, you need not give me any contribution. Its YOUR data.
You can contact me using my personal email id.

Disclaimer: Pls note that this is not marketing or business. I want to share my expertise and skill to the needed (As you know, I have been answering in this forum for the topics I am familiar with). However, I don't want to invite SPAMMERS or JUNK. Price for this service is meant to invite genuine researchers only. Some of the money raised will go in developing additional online resources for methylation analysis. The same has been posted on my blog  <http://chitka-kalyan.blogspot.fi/2014/12/extending-methylkit-christmas-offer-for.html> and also on r-bloggers.com <http://r-bloggers.com>

Regards,
Kalyan
